A Gaussian 20 mas East and 10 mas South of the phase centre, regridded from 3 mas (odd grid) to 5 mas (the fit's grid): the flux is the source's within the field to 1e-12, the centroid is where it was to 0.05 mas, East is still East (columns) and North North (rows).

The fit's field is smaller than the CLEAN's: the flux is that of the source pixels inside it (a source outside contributes none). Upsampling a plane from 10 mas to 5 mas is bilinear-exact (the coarse-to-fine step), to 1e-12 away from the edge.

``crosscheck.alma_maxent.convolve`` of a point source with an elliptical beam is ``alma_clean.gaussian_image`` (the kernel of CLEAN's ``restore``) at the same PA: the start image is smoothed with the beam CLEAN restored with, not its mirror image.

From a CLEAN directory: the image is what ``image_of`` returns from (log_brightness, flux) to 1e-12, every pixel is at least the floor, the flux is the field's flux plus the floor's, the small kernel (default) keeps the long baselines' power (a peak above the beam-smoothed one).
``build_problem(fixed_log_brightness=...)``: no ``log_brightness`` prior, and the data term and MPoL's entropy at the same values equal the free problem's, to 1e-12 (the held image is used by both).

``fit --workflow clean`` on synthetic data: stages selfcal (the image held: no ``log_brightness`` moves) then all, the start is the CLEAN image (no C9 Gaussian, no MPoL start), result.json holds the start's numbers, the self-calibration check and the usual report.

Spy on ``run_fit_c8``: the selfcal stage's problem has no ``log_brightness`` site, its nuisances move off their start, and the next stage starts from exactly the CLEAN start's image (``eta``) and the self-calibrated nuisances, then frees the image.

A fit with reference observation 3 (its gain 1) is renormalised to obs 0 = 1 before the range test and before picking obs 5, 6: the same physical gains give the same check from the ref-0 and the ref-3 parametrisations.

-ln L is invariant under g -> g / g_k, flux -> flux g_k; S_M is not. ``r_objective(entropy_flux=...)`` gives the ref-k fit the entropy of the same image in obs 0's gauge, so its objective equals the ref-0 parametrisation's; without it the entropies differ.

A per-observation bound (virgil's own): an offset at 90 % of a tight bound warns although it is 9 % of the loosest; the offsets' rows are the observations but the reference, so with reference 2 the rows name obs 0, 1, 3.
``image_only``: the fit's sites are the image and the flux; its data term equals the full problem's at gains 1, offsets 0, s = 1 (1e-12).

The model at observation e is flux g_e: after ``gauge_to_obs0`` the products are the same to 1e-15, obs 0 has gain 1 and offset 0, the offsets differ from the fit's by the one shift o_0; with ref_obs 0 the result is the fit's own.

``--ref-obs auto --offset-bound-mas 100``: result.json holds the resolved reference observation and its weights, the 3-beam proxy bound of every observation against the bound in force; the saved fit reports again (``report``) in the same gauge.

``cv-task`` builds the problem with reference observation 0: an init whose result.json says another one would put its n - 1 gains and offsets on the wrong observations, so it is refused before anything is fitted.

The flags of the release arms are accepted together: the CLEAN start (``--workflow clean``) with Adam, Toeplitz chi^2 and a decaying lr schedule, and the classic-MEM arm (``--taper-mas 0``) with Adam and Toeplitz, all on small synthetic data; Adam's lr schedule needs virgil#562, so those runs are skipped without it.

``--lam-m 3e-10`` is lam_R = 2 N lambda_M = 0.025452679 at N = 42,421,131 (the default lambda_M = 1e-9 gives 0.0848...); ``--lam 1e-9`` (a lambda_M given as lam_R, which turns the entropy off) and ``--lam`` with ``--lam-m`` are refused.

``entropy_on="base"`` (MEM's intrinsic correlation function, Gull 1989): the entropy term is ``mpol_entropy_jax(taper_mas=0)`` of the base image, the data term is that of the default problem (the model keeps its 30 mas kernel, so the model visibilities are unchanged), and the default ``"blurred"`` is the entropy of the blurred image, as before; with ``taper_mas=0`` the two coincide.
The bright source is at (+300, +100) mas and the faint one at (-200, -400) mas, to one pixel, in both spectral windows.

CASA's DATA is the complex conjugate of V = sum F exp(-2 pi i (u x + v y)) at u = +UVW[0] nu / c (equivalently V at (-u, -v)): the `read` default (conjugate=True) matches the point-source model to float32 precision.

The wrong mapping, V = DATA at +u (conjugate=False), mirrors the sky through the phase centre: the bright peak lands at (-300, -100) and the visibilities miss the model by about twice their amplitude.
u = UVW[0] nu / c: the longest baseline of the 8-antenna layout (about 1.6 km) at 230 GHz is 1.0-1.3 Mlambda, and u scales with nu.
visread (the reader MPoL uses; it also conjugates DATA) gives the same samples, to float32 precision.

With 1 mJy simple noise on each of XX and YY, the polarization-averaged visibility has sigma = 1 mJy / sqrt 2 on each of Re and Im, weight w1 + w2 = 2e6 Jy^-2; the successive-difference estimate of s is 1 within 3 standard errors, and the scatter about the known model agrees.
16800 cross-correlation rows per window, 4 channels: stride 7 keeps rows 0, 7, 14, ... (2400 rows).
A sample is kept only if FLAG_ROW is false, neither parallel-hand correlation is flagged and both weights are positive.
The reader is for one pointing: a two-field MS needs `field`, which then selects its rows only.
Without the column the reader uses WEIGHT (and says so); with a WEIGHT_SPECTRUM that differs by channel it uses that, and says so.
V = F exp(-2 pi i (u x + v y)) inverts to F at (x, y): +East is column 0 side, +North is row 0 side, and the peak value is the flux.
Points at cell centres have no gridding error: the FFT route equals the DFT.
Off-cell points are moved to the nearest cell: the image peak stays at the source and its height is reduced, never increased.
Weights 4 times too large (sigma underestimated by 2) give s^2 = 4.
A slow drift between integrations adds to |dV|^2: s^2 > 1, the bias the docs bound with the short-baseline data.
Each pixel is a point at its centre: the separable sum equals the sum of the closed-form point-source visibilities, at off-centre pixels on a non-square grid.
d/dI[r, c] of F = Re sum_k conj(a_k) V_k(I) is the adjoint sum with z = conj(a), checked against central differences of ``image_visibilities``.

Stage 0 of the GP plan: ``Image(MultipoleField)`` (no taper, gains, offsets and per-ddid sigma free, reference observation fixed) at a random latent: the Toeplitz loss equals the direct one to 1e-8 relative, and so does every gradient leaf (latent, sigma, flux, gains, offsets, sigmas) to 1e-8 of its own largest component.

Control, on the engine side: the Toeplitz term is evaluated at the main test's values with one realistic mistake (offsets sign-flipped, offsets shifted by 0.5 mas, one observation's gain changed by 1e-4) while the direct term keeps the true values; the main test's comparison then fails at its own 1e-8, in the value or in the gradient (the gain's gradient, the offsets' gradient), so a Toeplitz engine that mishandled the spread offsets or the gains would be caught.

Stage 1 holds gains, offsets and sigmas: its term at (latent, sigma, flux) equals the free problem's at the same values with those held, in loss and in the gradient of the fitted sites; the held sites are not parameters.

The measuring helper is first pinned against ``crosscheck.alma_clean.gaussian_image``, which documents that layout, so the check does not rest on the helper's own convention.

Control: a field at ``pa`` = 54.5 deg (the minor-axis reading of 144.5) has its major axis 90 deg from 144.5, far outside the 1 deg of the check; so does the mirror image (360 - 144.5 = 215.5, i.e. 35.5 deg), the opposite handedness.

At random image and nuisance values on the IM Lup subsample (128^2 pixels at 5 mas, 30 mas taper), the R objective -ln L + lam_R S_M at lam_R = 2 N lam_M (C4) equals 2 N (neg_log_likelihood_avg + lam_M entropy) of the example's own Net and mpol.losses (accurate NuFFT), to 1e-5 of the model-dependent part (the constants cancel). lam_M = 1e-5 makes the penalty several times |nll|, so that 1e-5 of the total pins S_M to 1e-5; the S_M alone agrees to the float32 of MPoL's taper buffer, and lam_M = 1e-9 (the paper's) is checked as well.

R2. ``fit --config R`` for 20 steps per stage at 128^2: the objective falls from the Gaussian start, the trajectory, stop reason, convergence verdict, per-ddid chi^2/N (s = 1 first), image, FITS and one residual dirty image per observation exist.

C3 in the fit itself. `fit`'s final loss minus r_objective (-ln L + lam S_M, outside `fit`) at the same values is a constant (the priors' normalisation), the same at lam = 0 and lam = 1; so `fit` adds lam S_M, with the plus sign. Control: a problem without the MPoLEntropy term has a different constant, by lam S_M, so the comparison does fail when the term is missing.

`score` (per-point decomposition, eps 1e-12) equals 1/2 sum r^2 + log_norm + sum (ln 2 pi - ln w) of the fit's own term, to 1e-12 relative, with and without a mask, and its per-ddid and per-annulus tallies add up.
C8 on a synthetic trajectory: a loss that changed by 0.05 over 200 steps has converged, one that changed by 5 has not; C13's acceptance rule on s / ŝ.

R4. ``compare`` of a fit with an MPoL export made from the same solution (mocked in W8's format: the 1028^2 grid is replaced by the fit's own): s = g s_M, gains, offsets, flux and the three image differences are zero and the two R objectives are equal (virgil at eps 1e-12 on both). With the export's gains 1% off, the gain difference is nonzero and the objective at MPoL's solution changes. This is plumbing: the mock shares the mapping's conventions, so it is not evidence about MPoL's export (W8's real one is).

``compare`` without ``--f-dir``/``--dsharp`` (R against MPoL alone): the per-ddid raw chi^2/N at both solutions, the objective term by term against MPoL's own numbers, gains and offsets side by side, and the gradient by parameter group, whose ``dx/dz`` of the offsets is half the offset bound (the sigmoid coordinate) while the pixels' is 1.

``mpol-init``: values.npz from MPoL's export equals ``values_from_mpol_export`` (image, flux, g, offsets in mas, s = g s_M); for an export made from our own fit it reproduces that fit's values, and ``fit --init`` of it starts at that objective and does not rise.

The DSHARP step of ``compare``, run as the command: the fit's image (here the R fit's, standing in for F's) convolved to a CLEAN beam and written as a 4-axis restored FITS with a hand-written header (East-left CDELT1, row 0 South, the phase centre in cell (N/2 - 1, N/2 - 1), so no repository WCS helper builds the header) gives ``F_vs_dsharp`` zero differences; the same FITS with its reference pixel shifted by 3 pixels, which is what an off-by-pixel WCS would do, does not.

Model evaluation in chunks of 37 points (every observation split many times, the last chunk short) gives the same per-point decomposition, tallies and dirty images as one call per observation, to 1e-12; and no chunk is larger than ``chunk_size``.

The fit's values, image (npy and fits) and a provisional result.json (stages, loss history, complete false) are on disk when the reporting step raises, as the out-of-memory did on the A100; ``report`` then writes the full result, equal to the one an uninterrupted fit writes, without refitting (its wall time is the fit's).

`fit` reporting converged (stop None) while the loss still falls by 50 is not C8: the loop restarts it, and stops only when the loss has changed by less than 0.1 over >= 100 steps, saying so. Controls: a loop that always gains runs to ``max_steps``, one that stalls stops with ``stalled`` and one out of time with ``time_limit``.

On a real (small) problem a loose ``gtol`` makes `fit` stop with stop None well short of the minimum; the C8 loop restarts it and reaches a lower loss, in more than one round, with C8 true or the step budget spent.
``precondition="diag"`` raises a clear error when ``virgil.fit`` has no such parameter (checked against a stub, so in every environment), and "none" and None are the same setting that needs nothing.

With a virgil that has ``precondition``, the C8 loop records the scaling's per-round stats (spread >= 0, floored fraction in [0, 1], at least one record per restart) and each restart's steps and wall time; without it, none.

Short rounds (30 steps each, loss still) are not C8 (window under 100 steps); a non-finite round stops the loop without calling ``on_round`` (no NaN save); a time limit already spent returns instead of raising; virgil's real ``time`` stop is what the loop maps to ``time_limit``.

`mpol_start_values` is uniform through our softmax parametrisation (zero logits, flux = value dx^2 npix^2): `image_of` returns one value in every pixel and the pixels sum to the flux, to 1e-12; gains 1, offsets 0, s = 1; the C9 start is not uniform. That the value is softplus(-3) and that sgd.py starts there is transcribed from mpol 0.3.1 images.py:65-76 and sgd.py:49-59 (cited in the design note), not checked against MPoL here.

On random complex data, model and weights, with g != 1 and s_M != 1: MPoL's `log_likelihood` = -(1/2 sum r^2 + log_norm) - sum_d (N_d ln 2 pi - sum_k ln w_k), with virgil's s = g s_M, to 1e-12 relative, and `neg_log_likelihood_avg` * 2N is -ln L as well.

The wrong map (virgil s = s_M, forgetting that MPoL also divides the weights by g^2) misses MPoL's log likelihood by 2 sum ln g plus a change of chi-squared: far more than rounding, so the 1e-12 test above pins s = g s_M.

MPoL's forward visibilities (torchkbnufft, the example's Net with its nuisance layers), virgil's `data.model` and a float64 numpy DFT, on the IM Lup uv of 10^4 points: virgil is exact to 1e-10 (NUFFT eps 1e-12); MPoL's table interpolation errs by 6e-4; and MPoL against virgil is within MPoL's own error, so the difference is its transform's, not a convention.

With `sparse_matrices=True`, MPoL's own more accurate option, the same model matches the exact DFT and virgil to 1e-5: the 6e-4 above is table interpolation, so every convention in the map (orientation, centre, offsets, taper, gains) is right to that level, not merely to 6e-4.

Dropping the half-pixel offset, or not reversing the columns (RA increases to the left), the rows, or both, makes virgil miss MPoL's visibilities (the accurate-NUFFT path, which the matched map reproduces to 1e-5) by more than 1e-3, up to order one: the agreement above pins the orientation and the phase centre. Simulate (numpy, exact DFT, Gaussian noise of variance 1/w in each of Re and Im, so that exp(-chi2/2) is the likelihood) 600 visibilities of a 16 x 16 image in three observations with injected offsets (3.1, -2.2) and (-1.7, 4.4) mas, flux 0.7 and gains 1.08, 0.93, and fit flux, gains and offsets (image known) with virgil's spread-offsets Toeplitz term and L-BFGS from flux 1, unit gains, zero offsets, on K = 16 noise realisations. The expected scatter is the Cramer-Rao one, the inverse of the Fisher information F of (flux, gains, offsets) from the reference's analytic derivatives (about 0.17 mas per offset component here; the maximum-likelihood estimator is unbiased and attains it to first order at this signal-to-noise). So: (a) d^2 = (theta_hat - theta)^T F (theta_hat - theta) ~ chi-squared with 7 degrees of freedom per fit, so its mean over K fits, divided by 7, is 1 +- sqrt(2 / (7 K)) = 0.134: accepted within 3 of those (0.40); (b) no bias: K times the Mahalanobis norm of the mean error is chi-squared with 7 dof, accepted below its 99.9% point (24.3); (c) no component more than 4.5 standard deviations off in any fit (two-sided probability 7e-6 per component, 112 components); (d) the fitted values equal the maximum likelihood of the numpy chi-squared (scipy BFGS, analytic gradient) from the same start to 1e-4 sigma in the Fisher metric, which is the exactness of the optimizer's stopping rule (the documented floor sqrt(eps) of the largest starting gradient per data point; measured 1e-5 sigma or less), so a wrong or biased spread term moves the estimate by order sigma, four orders above.
